current.critique: As it stands, the wing that remembers every crash still has the strong clip: the replay of the soft tip curling just before the dive, with an aeroelastic coupling checked against a cantilever so it cannot be faked with a mass offset. The two faults from last round are still open. The crash names the spot and the splint goes there, so the player follows instructions more than they decide. And the loop converges: once the weak places are stiff the wing just works, the far island ends it, and 'flies further than any fresh one' only holds while fresh wings stay crude. The Learn to Fly shadow keeps memorable where it is.

goals.title: Sparks from stones
goals.critique: This is the human's direction at its most literal: real materials, a general field solver, parts fitted by hand. It answers the convergence fault of the wing rounds, because the parts feed back into every machine built before. The misbuilt motor wrenching itself off the bench and the nail flying to the stone are honest, unscripted clips, and the road starts with something to play with on day one (a magnet stone every iron thing feels). The weak side: it is close to the human's own example, so it is the least surprising pick, and circuit-and-wire sandboxes are well-trodden ground, so memorable rests entirely on the fields being real. A motor needs Biot-Savart over wound turns, contact-based commutation through brushes, Joule heating and rigid bodies all stable at play rate. Each of those is a place where a scripted torque would quietly turn 'nothing scripted' into a lie. The pitch also never says what the player does minute to minute while Lumi's beak winds the coil, as opposed to watching it.

goals.title: Every wing is answered by its sky
goals.critique: This is the wing again, but it fixes both faults named last round, so it earns more than a reword. Every fix now has a price (weight, drag, sink), and skies that no single wing can master stop the loop from converging. The result is a shelf of named wings and a real choice for each day's wind. The friend's own mass as a passenger is a better reason to rebuild than ballast ever was. The weak side: the thermal, the gust and the calm reach need honest wind fields under a coupled aeroelastic wing, which is the most fakeable physics on the island, and the Learn to Fly shadow is still there. It is also a sixth wing round, sitting on one material pair (cane and paper) while the human asks for a world where everything can be worked.

goals.title: Toys the friends wear out
goals.critique: Wear that stays on the toy and friends who break things at their weak spot give the creatures a real part in the test. A playroom full of broken history is a warm idea. But a spinning-top battle is familiar ground, the boat and the tops reuse things already built, and the pitch is three separate toys with no machine that grows. The 'friends play by physics' half needs creatures that handle objects convincingly, which the pitch takes for granted. Without it, the play becomes a timer that breaks the toy.
